title: Generalization of Pearl's Front-Door Criterion
summary: Pearl's front-door criterion provides a set of sufficient conditions for estimating the total causal effect from observational data in the presence of latent confounding, using the functional P(y | do(x := x*)) = \sum_z P(z | x*) \sum_x P(y | x, z) P(x). An open question is whether these conditions can be generalized to be both necessary and sufficient for the validity of this functional, similar to the generalization achieved for the back-door adjustment criterion by Shpitser.
